name: Animal Welfare Reading List
description: A curated, annotated library of writing, research, and data on animal welfare.
introduction: A curated, annotated library of the best writing, research, and data on animal welfare.

categories.title: Sentience and moral consideration
categories.description: What conscious experience is, which animals may have it, and why their experiences matter.

categories.title: Scale and global data
categories.description: Sources for understanding how many animals are affected and how those estimates are produced.

categories.title: Farmed animals
categories.description: Research and reporting on the lives of animals in food systems and the institutions around them.

categories.title: Aquatic animals
categories.description: Counts, capture methods, farming, and welfare for animals often recorded only by weight.

categories.title: Wild animals
categories.description: The welfare of free-living animals, including suffering from natural causes and human activity.

categories.title: Animals used in research
categories.description: Official records of animal use in science and the severity assigned to experimental procedures.

categories.title: Reasoning about suffering
categories.description: Evidence on severe pain, treatments, and the institutions that determine which treatments are studied.

categories.title: Possible futures
categories.description: Proposals for using greater knowledge and technological capacity to reduce suffering more radically.

entries.name: New York Declaration on Animal Consciousness
entries.annotation: A concise statement of scientific agreement. It reports strong support for conscious experience in mammals and birds, and at least a realistic possibility in all vertebrates and many invertebrates, including insects, cephalopods, and decapod crustaceans.
entries.reuse: Publicly readable; no general reuse license is stated.

entries.name: Animal Consciousness
entries.annotation: A scholar-maintained introduction to animal consciousness. It explains the concepts, history, evidence, methodological disputes, and ethical stakes, then points into an extensive scientific and philosophical bibliography.
entries.reuse: Free to read; Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy copyright applies.

entries.name: Searching for Animal Sentience
entries.annotation: A systematic review of 2,562 studies published from 1990 to 2012. Nearly all assumed the animals had the emotion or sentience-related trait being studied; only 16 investigated whether it existed. The review also shows how strongly the literature favored vertebrates and negative states such as fear, stress, and pain.
entries.access: Full-text HTML, PDF, and article metadata

entries.name: Sentience Institute
entries.annotation: Research on moral-circle expansion and social change. Its animal-focused work studies how institutions and public attitudes have changed toward farmed animals, and why moral concern reaches some beings while excluding others.
entries.evidence_type: Research reports and historical case studies
entries.access: Public HTML reports and downloadable data
entries.reuse: Check the terms attached to individual reports and datasets.

entries.name: Animal Welfare at Our World in Data
entries.annotation: The best single entry point to Our World in Data’s animal-welfare work. It gathers writing, charts, and downloadable data on slaughter, factory farming, housing systems, aquatic animals, pain, and public attitudes.
entries.evidence_type: Topic synthesis, articles, charts, and datasets
entries.access: Public HTML, downloadable CSV and JSON, chart API
entries.reuse: OWID writing, charts, and OWID-produced data are generally CC BY 4.0; third-party data retain their source terms.

references.label: How many animals are slaughtered every day?

entries.name: FAOSTAT and fisheries statistics
entries.annotation: The primary international source for country-reported livestock, slaughter, fisheries, and aquaculture statistics. Many later estimates begin with FAO records, including attempts to convert aquatic-animal tonnage into individual animals.
entries.access: Interactive databases, bulk downloads, and APIs
entries.reuse: FAO database terms and source-specific conditions apply.

entries.name: Faunalytics research library
entries.annotation: A large, continually updated collection of research summaries and original studies. It spans animals used for food and science, wild and companion animals, public attitudes, and the effectiveness of attempts to help animals.
entries.reuse: Publicly readable; check item-level terms before reuse.

entries.name: Animal Clock
entries.annotation: A real-time counter that turns annual estimates of animals killed for food in the United States into rates. It includes land animals and estimated wild-caught and farmed aquatic animals.
entries.reuse: No general reuse license is stated.

entries.name: Sentient Media
entries.annotation: Independent reporting and explainers on factory farming, fisheries, animal welfare, food systems, climate, health, and policy. It combines current investigations with accessible background pieces on how animal industries operate.
entries.access: Public HTML without an account or paywall; ordinary article crawling is allowed by robots.txt.
entries.reuse: All rights reserved; reproduction, distribution, transmission, and caching require prior written permission.

entries.name: Inside Animal Ag
entries.annotation: A research-based guide to the structure and effects of U.S. factory farming. Its linked subject guides cover animal numbers and treatment alongside slaughterhouses, industry structure, workers, public health, government, land, water, climate, and biodiversity.
entries.access: Public HTML; robots.txt permits crawling with a delay.

entries.name: Welfare Footprint Project
entries.annotation: A framework for comparing welfare through the intensity and duration of negative experiences and the number of animals affected. Its applied studies estimate cumulative time spent in pain under different production systems.
entries.evidence_type: Quantitative welfare framework and applied research
entries.reuse: Check the terms attached to individual publications.

entries.name: Fishcount
entries.annotation: The main source for estimates of individual fish caught from the wild and produced in aquaculture. Fishcount converts tonnage into animal counts and documents welfare problems during capture, transport, and slaughter.
entries.access: Public HTML reports, tables, and downloadable documents
entries.reuse: Check the terms attached to individual estimates and publications.

entries.name: Sea Around Us
entries.annotation: A research initiative that reconstructs marine catches by country, taxon, fishing sector, and destination. Its estimates include discards, small-scale fishing, and unreported catch often missing from official landings.
entries.access: Public HTML, interactive data, and downloads
entries.reuse: Project citation and data-use terms apply.

entries.name: Wild Animal Initiative
entries.annotation: The leading research organization focused specifically on the welfare of free-living animals. Its work develops field methods, reviews welfare-relevant ecology, maps research priorities, and supports the growth of wild-animal welfare science.
entries.evidence_type: Research program, reviews, and field methods
entries.access: Public HTML research library and papers
entries.reuse: Check the terms attached to individual publications.

entries.name: Wild Animal Welfare Committee
entries.annotation: An independent UK committee examining the welfare of free-living animals affected by human activity. Its publications show how welfare evidence can change decisions about wildlife management, conservation, conflict, and population control.
entries.evidence_type: Independent expert analysis and policy advice
entries.reuse: Check the terms attached to individual publications.

entries.name: EU Animals in Science and ALURES
entries.annotation: The European Commission’s transparency system for animals used in scientific procedures. It reports species, numbers, purposes, origins, genetic status, and the severity assigned to procedures across EU member states and Norway.
entries.evidence_type: Official regional statistics and project records
entries.access: Public dashboards and full dataset exports
entries.reuse: European Commission reuse rules and dataset-specific notices apply.

entries.name: Psychedelics and cluster headache
entries.annotation: A readable overview of Yale’s clinical research on psilocybin, LSD, and DMT for cluster headache, a disorder defined by attacks of extreme pain. It explains early findings and ongoing studies without presenting psychedelics as established cures.
entries.reuse: Free to read; Yale University copyright applies.

entries.name: The Hedonistic Imperative
entries.annotation: David Pearce’s long-running argument that biotechnology could eventually replace suffering with gradients of well-being in humans and nonhuman animals. The archive connects genetics, consciousness, animal ethics, and the future redesign of ecosystems.

entries.name: Herbivorize Predators
entries.annotation: A speculative proposal to use directed evolution to let predatory species survive without killing other animals.
entries.reuse: No general reuse license is stated.
